text:
alex: Anyone else seeing a weird tail-latency spike on the shared GPU pool around 11:03? Small prompts suddenly jumped to ~1s+ p99.
maria: Yup saw it. 11:02–11:06 window. Grafana shows p50 steady but p99 spikes only on pool-b shared.
devon: I pulled a flamegraph. Looks like we triggered a kernel autoswitch on several nodes around that time. Kernel 42 -> 17.
alex: Right — I grabbed the runtime logs: \n```
2026-03-17T18:02:58Z kernel_select: chosen=42 reason=default
2026-03-17T18:03:05Z kernel_select: chosen=17 reason=autotune(throughput)
2026-03-17T18:03:05Z request: tenant=acme_job id=xyz seq_len=24 batch=1
2026-03-17T18:03:05Z perf: kernel17 latency_ms=9.8 mean for seq<=64
```
maria: Kernel 17 is our high-throughput kernel tuned for long sequences; it reduces register usage but increases startup overhead. For short seq it actually has worse latency.
sylvia: That matches profiling I ran yesterday. Kernel 17 has ~3x tail latency for seq<=32 compared to kernel 42. devon do you have numbers?
devon: Quick summary from perf-run: for seq<=64, kernel42 p99=210ms, kernel17 p99=920ms. For seq>=512, kernel42 p99=2.1s, kernel17 p99=1.2s. So autoswitch heuristic favored throughput without considering seq distribution.
ken: Which tenant caused the flip? ops can we throttle or isolate? ops: The flip correlated with a burst from tenant acme_job launching a long-context batch of 1024 tokens. They landed on same GPUs in pool-b as multiple small-req tenants.
alex: So noisy neighbour: long-seq tenant causes selector to favor kernel17 and everybody else suffers.
maria: Also noticed KV-cache churn. The long requests populate large KV slots and cause eviction pressure, increasing overhead for subsequent short requests.
devon: I dumped kv cache stats: eviction spike at 18:03:08, avg cache lookup time increased 15%.
infra-bot: alert: shared-pool-high-p99-latency created by monitor at 2026-03-17T18:03:11Z (severity=medium)
ken: Immediate mitigation: pin the long-context tenant to dedicated pool or apply soft per-tenant kernel policy. Can we do a quick sticky-route for acme_job to dedicated? ops: I can move them if they consent; they are in trial though.
sylvia: Short-term patch idea: change kernel selector to consider median request seq length over last N seconds per-GPU, not just global throughput metric. Also add a hard cutoff: don't switch to kernel17 if fraction_short_requests > 0.6.
alex: I opened a quick hotfix PR to require median_seq_len >= 256 before switching to throughput-optimized kernels. PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/ka/PR-4821
maria: Also propose adding a per-tenant kernel override flag (tenant_metadata.kernel_preference = {prefer_low_latency:true}) so customers can opt-in to low-latency profile.
devon: For immediate relief, we can restart selector on nodes in pool-b to revert to kernel42. But that's disruptive. Alternative: temp throttle batch_size for long-seq jobs OR apply tenant-weighted kernel score that penalizes switching if active small-req tenants > X.
ken: Ops ran a soft throttle on acme_job (reduced concurrency) at 18:07. p99 dropped from ~1.2s to ~280ms over next 3 minutes.
ops: Confirmed. We also pinned acme_job off the busiest 2 nodes as a stopgap.
sylvia: Follow-up action items: \n- devon: run a simulated mixed workload test with the new selector thresholds (N=60s window) and post perf matrix.
- maria: add KV-cache eviction metrics to the failure dashboard so we can correlate next time.
- ken/ops: coordinate with acme to schedule either dedicated or reduced concurrency.
- alex: ship the hotfix PR to canary.
alex: Canary rollout started at 18:45 on 2 nodes. No regressions observed so far. Monitoring dashboard: small-req p99 returned to baseline.
devon: Recorded a profiling artifact: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/2007654321-kernel-switch-profiles.tar.gz (contains pprof + nvtx traces). Put a short glue script in the PR to reproduce.
maria: Longer-term: update autoscaler + selector to use multi-dimensional cost: latency_impact = w1*median_seq + w2*short_fraction + w3*active_tenants_short. Autoscale policies should also respect tenant labels (e.g., latency_SLA).
ken: Agree. Also consider per-tenant max_kernel_switch_per_hour to avoid flip-flops.
ops: For postmortem I'll capture timeline and mitigations. Low-level root cause: kernel autoswitch + co-located long-seq tenant + KV eviction pressure.
alex: Thanks everyone. Good triage. If no objections I'll close the incident ticket after ops posts the postmortem. :thumbsup:
maria: No objections. Add retrospective note to eng-runtime retro next Tues.
devon: I'll upload the perf graphs and attach to the postmortem.
infra-bot: incident-2007654321 closed by ops at 2026-03-17T19:12:05Z
